correctness.rationale: For tree bond percolation, seed-to-target reachability equals p to unique path length. Exact all-labelled Prüfer generation, exact complete canonical-tree-isomorphism sorting and integer coefficient nonnegativity certificates establish universal optimal vertices for every tree with at most seven nodes and 21 of 23 eight-node types. Disjoint rational parameter optimizers disprove universality in two remaining types. Independently displayed exact polynomials prove sharp switching values and full optima, all checked by the packaged executable.

evidence: Holme arxiv:1708.06456 uses continuous-time Markov SIR and studies node rankings for connected graphs through seven vertices. Although joint outgoing transmissions are dependent, the probability of each unique tree infection path is p to its length at matched p, making the mean tree vaccination objective equivalent.
Hall–Siebert doi:10.1007/s00285-022-01854-9 proves Markovian SIR/SEIR node-probability formulas for trees with a unique seed; no optimizer census or threshold is given.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For continuous-time Markov SIR on a tree with constant infection rate beta and recovery rate gamma, distinct infectors along one seed-to-target path have independent infectious durations; hence the path probability is (beta/(beta+gamma)) to its length. Therefore Holme’s mean tree objective coincides with the independent-edge expectation and supplies closely related earlier coverage through seven vertices. Its stated results do not enumerate eight-vertex trees or imply precisely two first-switching exceptions; Hall–Siebert likewise offers no optimization census.

originality.rationale: Full primary-source comparisons acknowledge that Markov SIR and independent-bond Reed–Frost have the same mean outbreak objective on trees after matching edge transmission probabilities; the contribution is the first-eight-tree vaccine-location switching classification beyond earlier seven-vertex calculations. Existing weighted distance-polynomial methods do not by themselves imply the sharp cutoff; closest local and published finding statements do not subsume it. Search limitations and alternative nomenclature are explicitly retained.
residual_risks: Unknown earlier vertex-deleted Wiener-polynomial extremal theorem or epidemiological vaccine-centrality table may imply the classification under different terminology.
The 2007 weighted Hosoya–Wiener full PDF was not retrieved and only its abstract was inspected; no whole-paper exclusion is claimed.
The 2022 site-bond vaccination study was available at abstract level only, so the noncoverage comparison is limited to that stated scope.
No independent publication-priority validation has been conducted.

value.rationale: The model asks a natural actionable question: which vertex should receive the only vaccine when edge transmissibility is uncertain? Determining the smallest tree requiring different optima at different p is a motivated finite cutoff; two fully classified shapes and exact p-switch thresholds expose a nontrivial tradeoff between high-degree hubs and network separators. The fact is not an arbitrary graph slice or a routine evaluation of known distance counts; the exhaustive first-switching threshold is the scientific claim.
